title: fix(storybook): stop metric cards story rendering blank
body:
## Problem

- Merge queue batches fail Visual Review when the metric cards story renders blank: 11 attempts on 9/23-24 ([example run](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/actions/runs/36007458653/job/107660322816)).
- The story reads its args with Storybook's `useArgs` hook.
- [`withKea`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/3aeb5771b77fbbc998ad43ff1e4fa9150aad1419/common/storybook/.storybook/decorators/withKea/kea-story.tsx#L59-L68) mounts the story one render late, after Storybook clears the hook context, so `useArgs` throws.

## Changes

- `CardsPreview`, a story-only fixture, keeps its own state in React `useState`. The story keys it by the args that seed that state. Nothing looks different.
- oxlint now rejects any import from `storybook/preview-api`, because every preview hook fails the same way under `withKea`. No other file imports it.
- The `metric-cards--interactive` baselines come back in `frontend/snapshots.yml`, with the same hashes as before. [add slash commands to the runner composer](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/105792) dropped them after the flake, so every queue batch since then has failed Visual Review on 2 `new` snapshots. The entries came through the Visual Review approve and finalize flow on this PR, not a hand edit.
- Not in scope: moving the `withKea` reset to `useLayoutEffect` would fix the timing for every story, but changes render order everywhere and needs a full visual regression run.

## How did you test this code?

- Ran `test-storybook` 5 times against a local static build, before and after.
  - Before: 5 of 5 runs failed the first `Interactive` attempt with "Storybook preview hooks can only be called inside decorators and story functions".
  - After: 0 of 5.
- The story buttons still toggle state in a headless browser.
- Not checked: the CI renderer.

## Release status

- [x] No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone <!-- release-status: fully-available -->

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5

- No duplicate: no open or recent PR touches this story or `useArgs`.
- Skills: /debugging-ci-failures, /writing-ui-components, /writing-code-comments, /reviewing-with-coderabbit, /writing-pr-descriptions, /code-review (medium, no findings), /simplify.
- /simplify moved the state into `CardsPreview` and widened the lint ban to the whole module.
- CodeRabbit and Greptile PR reviews: one shared note, that clicking a card no longer updates the Storybook controls panel. Rejected, because syncing args back needs `useArgs`, the hook this PR removes.
- CodeRabbit thread on `CardsPreview.tsx`, asking for a kea logic per `.cursor/rules/react-typescript.mdc`: rejected and resolved. `frontend/src/AGENTS.md` sets no such rule, 343 product frontend files use `useState`, and the fixture has one story consumer.
- CodeRabbit CLI, without `--deep`: fixed stale state after a control change. Rejected 2 findings asking for a kea logic, because 165 story files already keep local state in `useState`.

<!-- Overall PR authoring rules for agents:
- Title: <type>(<scope>): <description> — type=feat|fix|chore, scope required, lowercase, no period, <72 chars.
  ✅ feat(insights): add retention graph export
  ❌ feat: Added retention export.   (capitalized, period, no scope)
- Description: high-level rationale, not a step-by-step replay.
- Voice: the subject of every sentence is the change, never its author. No "I", "me" or "my" anywhere in the body. "I (actually Claude)" is worse than either half: it hands the assignee an account of work they did not do. Authorship is one stated fact in the Agent context section below.
- Body: pass it straight to the creation tool's `body` arg (GitHub MCP `create_pull_request` body, or `gh pr create --body-file -` via stdin) — don't write it to a temp file first; the arg preserves markdown and newlines verbatim.
- Flow and topology changes: include separate before-and-after Mermaid `flowchart` blocks with PostHog colors. This includes CI wiring, pipelines, state machines, and request paths. Use `/writing-pr-descriptions` for the palette and role mapping.
- Public OSS repo: no internal customers, incidents, or operational metrics.
- Stack instead of stuffing: if the diff holds two or more separable steps (migration then behavior, rename then rewrite), open a stack rather than one big PR. See AGENTS.md, "Stacked PRs" and /stacking-prs.
- Simplify before opening: if your agent has a behavior-preserving cleanup pass (Claude Code: `/simplify`), run it on a non-trivial diff before final tests and preflight, since it edits the tree. Skip it for small mechanical changes.
- Review before opening: invoke `/reviewing-with-coderabbit` once over the branch. If the CLI is unavailable, open the PR anyway.
- Draft by default: open new PRs as drafts (`gh pr create --draft`) — drafts run only a narrow CI subset and save runner credits. Fix CI and run affected tests locally before marking ready for review.
- Labels: apply `skip-agent-review` for trivial/chore PRs that don't need Copilot or Greptile review.
- When a human directed the work, the PR must be attributable to that person, even if agent-assisted.
- If a human directed this work, assign them as the PR assignee (the DRI) — actually set the assignee, don't just name them here. Leave a PR unassigned only when it is fully autonomous with no human driver (set Autonomy to "Fully autonomous").
- Never write a GitHub @mention or username you have not verified this session. Resolve a real handle from `gh api user` (current user) or the PR's actual author/assignee via `gh pr view --json author,assignees` — never infer a handle from a display name.
- Do not add a human Co-authored-by just for the sake of attribution — if no human was involved in the changes, own it as agent-authored.
- Agent-authored PRs always require human review — do not self-merge or auto-approve.
- Do NOT claim manual testing you haven't done.
- Shape and style: invoke the `/writing-pr-descriptions` skill before writing this body. In short: lead with the effect a person sees rather than the code path behind it, make the body stand alone for a reader who opens no files, size it to the change, link evidence rather than asserting what CI already reports, then hold what's left to one fact per bullet in under 25 words. A body that got longer as bullets was not cut.
